medium.description: Status line reports 'worker wait' forever under the normal non-crossOriginIsolated serving path. The status reads R.workerResults (index.html:173), but graph-view.js render loop clears workerResults when the worker posts an ArrayBuffer ('if (s instanceof ArrayBuffer) n.workerResults = null;'), which is exactly the path sim.js takes without SharedArrayBuffer. Verification's browser.dom_status 'worker wait' is therefore expected even though drag proves the worker is alive. The status is not a reliable health signal.

Async renderer/worker failures are invisible. poll() only wraps the synchronous init() call (194-198); the vendored renderer defers initGraphics in a 50 ms setTimeout and retries once in another setTimeout (graph-view.js:319-326), and the worker has no 'error' handler (graph-view.js:313). If the second graphics init throws or vendor/sim.js fails to load, the page can keep showing 'ready · nodes 9 · links 10' over a blank canvas with the #error overlay still display:none.

Test harness can record PASS for checks that did not actually assert success: check() records PASS for any non-throwing callback and only returns Boolean(detail && detail.ok) without using it (48-55). Separately, vendored-sha256-verbatim records SKIP for a missing source and still records the aggregate PASS (233-235), so if /home/erema/obsidian-graph is absent the smoke test can exit 0 with zero real byte comparisons. Current run has all sources, but the test is not hermetic.

Static-root containment is lexical, not physical. resolveRequestPath uses path.resolve (118) and fsp.stat/readFile (160, 182), which follow symlinks; a symlink placed under web/ could serve a file outside STATIC_ROOT despite the '..' checks. No symlinks exist today, so it is not exploitable in the current tree, but the safety guarantee is weaker than the comments imply.

No assertion that the Worker is actually the 4th Renderer argument. The regex only checks that 'new Worker(...vendor/sim.js...)' appears somewhere in index.html (255-257); a regression that constructs the Worker but passes undefined to Renderer would still pass the smoke test, even though the engine would then load bare 'sim.js' and break.

low.description: Unused import: const fs = require('node:fs') is never referenced (only fsp is used). Dead code.
shutdown(signal) accepts a signal but never uses it; SIGINT and SIGTERM take identical paths.
-h is aliased to --host, so 'node bin/server.js -h' throws '--host requires a value' instead of printing help; only --help works. Minor CLI UX trap.
DEMO_WEIGHTS and DEMO_LINKS are hand-maintained and can drift from DEMO_NODES; only the final 9/10 counts are asserted at 160-166, not per-node degree or link-target integrity.
Security headers (nosniff) are set only on 200 responses; 4xx/5xx text responses omit them. Low impact for a localhost static server.

recommendations: Add worker.onerror and window 'error'/'unhandledrejection' listeners that call fatal(), and surface the first worker message as a real health flag instead of inferring health from R.workerResults.
Change the status text to distinguish 'worker ready' from 'worker ack received'; do not print 'worker wait' indefinitely for the ArrayBuffer transfer path.
Make tests/stage0-smoke.js fail when any original source file is missing (or require an explicit --allow-missing-source flag), and make check() honor an {ok:false} return value.
Resolve request paths with fs.realpath and re-check containment against STATIC_ROOT to close the symlink escape.
Add a smoke assertion that the new Worker(...) expression is the 4th argument of new Renderer(...), not merely present in the HTML.
Remove the unused node:fs import and unused shutdown(signal) parameter; decide whether -h should mean help or host and document it.
Consider recording reference-tree integrity with a checksum manifest or VCS, since /home/erema/obsidian-graph is not a git repository and the 'reference untouched' check cannot be diff-proven.
